Series::logical_xor¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::logical_xor(const Series& rhs) const -> Series

What It Does¶

logical_xor() returns true exactly where one side is truthy and the other is not.

This is the exclusive version of logical_or(): it does not reward both sides being true at once.

Parameters¶

rhs (const Series&)

The right-hand truth-value operand. It may broadcast against self.

Numeric inputs are interpreted by truthiness before the exclusive-or is computed.

Returns¶

Series A boolean Series whose lanes are true only where the aligned truth values differ.

Examples¶

Example 1. Numeric truthiness works exactly the way boolean masks do: zero is false, non-zero is true.

auto a = pluss::make_series({0, 2, 0, -5}, pluss::ScalarType::Int32);
auto b = pluss::make_series({1, 0, 3, 0}, pluss::ScalarType::Int32);

pluss::series::print(std::cout, a.logical_xor(b));

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[true, true, true, true]

Lane by lane, each pair has exactly one truthy member:

  • (0, 1) -> false xor true -> true

  • (2, 0) -> true xor false -> true

  • (0, 3) -> false xor true -> true

  • (-5, 0) -> true xor false -> true

Example 2. Two truthy values are not exclusive, so their lane becomes false.

auto left = pluss::make_series({0, 2, 0, -5}, pluss::ScalarType::Int32);
auto right = pluss::make_series({1, 0, 3, 0}, pluss::ScalarType::Int32);
std::cout << left.logical_xor(right);

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[true, true, true, true]

In this specific set every pair has exactly one non-zero value. Replacing the second pair with (2, 1) would make that lane false because both are truthy.

Example 3. Broadcasting uses the same shape contract as the other logical binary methods.

try {
  auto matrix = pluss::make_series({{true, false}, {true, false}},
                                   pluss::ScalarType::Bool);
  std::cout << matrix.logical_xor(
      pluss::make_series({true, false, true}, pluss::ScalarType::Bool));
} catch (const std::exception& error) { std::cout << error.what(); }

Output¶

broadcast: incompatible shapes

Gradient¶

Exclusive-or creates boolean control information. It does not provide a numeric derivative through the truth-value conversion.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • If both sides are true, the result is false.

  • If both sides are false, the result is also false.

  • Numeric inputs use truthiness, not exact 0/1 semantics.

Summary¶

Use logical_xor() when the interesting case is disagreement between two conditions.

See Also¶

  • Series::logical_or: true when either side is truthy.

  • Series::logical_and: true only when both sides are truthy.

  • Series::bitwise_xor: bit-pattern difference instead of truth-value difference.
